prompt:
Use case: product-mockup
Asset type: square unit icon sample for a historically grounded WWII strategy game.
Primary request: a photorealistic macro product photograph of a museum-grade physical scale model. Convincing miniature materials and accurate engineering, absolutely not a vector icon, flat drawing, cartoon, low-poly toy or illustration.
Scene/backdrop: seamless neutral charcoal studio background, subtly lighter behind the subject, no scenery, no text, no badge, no UI frame.
Composition/framing: one complete miniature centered, three-quarter view from above, its long axis diagonally across the square, front toward lower left, fill 85 percent of the frame with safe margins around all extremities. Focus stacking, entire model sharply in focus, no tilt-shift blur. Distinct silhouette readable when reduced to 40px.
Lighting/mood: large softbox upper left, restrained rim light, realistic ambient occlusion and contact shadows. Sober military museum photography.
Materials/textures: physically realistic painted metal, restrained paint wear at edges, fine panel seams, precise subtle weathering; no exaggerated rust, no glossy plastic, no thick outlines, no saturation boost.
Constraints: historically plausible WWII equipment, no modern weapons, no fantasy embellishments, no watermark, no labels, no decorative border. One object only.

Subject: a North American P-51D Mustang 1:48 museum scale model. Single piston engine in the nose with one FOUR-BLADED propeller, single vertical tail, bubble canopy, low-mounted straight tapered wings (not swept), characteristic belly radiator scoop. Natural aluminum skin with olive-drab anti-glare panel, subtle WWII US star-and-bar insignia. Wings intact, correct proportions, no jets. Landing gear retracted, a discreet dark display support under the belly blending into the background; no broad pedestal hiding the silhouette. Camera reveals nose, canopy, upper wing surfaces and tail.

Subject: a Boeing B-17G Flying Fortress 1:72 museum scale model. Exactly FOUR radial engine nacelles and FOUR three-bladed propellers, two engines per wing. Long slender fuselage, large broad wings, single tall vertical tail, glazed bombardier nose, defining twin-gun chin turret below nose, dorsal turret and ball turret where visible. Olive-drab upper surfaces and neutral-gray underside, restrained WWII US star-and-bar insignia. Landing gear retracted, discreet dark belly support blending into background. Accurately depict a heavy four-engine bomber, never a twin-engine aircraft or jet. All four engines and complete wing tips visible.

Subject: a Soviet IS-2 model 1944 heavy tank 1:35 museum scale model. Correct low cast rounded turret, very long 122 mm D-25T cannon with prominent double-baffle muzzle brake, sloped front hull, wide steel tracks, SIX large road wheels per side. Olive 4BO green paint with light edge wear, cast armor texture, weld beads, hatch and engine-deck detail. Tank and gun both point toward lower left, full barrel remains inside frame. Tracks rest directly on charcoal studio surface; no toy display stand, no earth diorama. Must be an IS-2, not a T-34, KV-2 or modern tank.

Subject: a WWII 1944 Iowa-class battleship 1:700 museum waterline scale model, completely visible from pointed bow to stern. Very long slender hull, THREE main turrets each with THREE 16-inch barrels, two turrets forward and one aft; wartime superstructure, two funnels, secondary enclosed twin five-inch gun mounts and period AA mounts. Blue-gray naval paint, muted wood deck. No missiles, no helicopters, no modern radar domes, no aircraft carrier deck. Tiny restrained dark resin-water plinth following the hull, subtle small ripples, no towering waves or action scene. Elevated bow-quarter viewpoint reveals full deck arrangement and all three main turrets; ship occupies almost full image diagonal without cropping.
